Research Program

Research & Projects

My research combines foundational ontological analysis with applied knowledge engineering. Rather than treating ontologies merely as domain vocabularies, I approach them as formal theories of invariance, causation, and change capable of grounding complex data ecosystems.

Core Research Lines

01 / Foundational Ontology

Events, Systems, and Dispositions

How are events delimited in time and space, and what anchors their identity when participants enter, exit, or undergo structural change? Originating from my doctoral theory on modeling events based on systems, this line of inquiry formalizes upper-level distinctions among occurrents, invariant systemic structures, dynamic participation, and causal dispositions.

02 / Semantic Interoperability & Digital Twins

Ontology Design Patterns for Complex Systems

Industrial and scientific infrastructures rely on heterogeneous data streams that must remain coherent across equipment replacements, state changes, and organizational boundaries. I develop modular domain ontologies and reusable Ontology Design Patterns (ODPs)—such as selective transitivity in flow networks and persistent functional locations—to support automated reasoning and digital twins.

03 / Neuro-Symbolic & AI-Assisted Ontology Engineering

Language Models and Formal Conceptual Grounding

Large Language Models excel at capturing linguistic plausibility, yet they lack explicit ontological commitments. I investigate methods that combine natural language definitions, vector representations, and top-level ontologies (such as BFO, UFO, and DOLCE) to classify domain entities, extract semantic relations, and build context-aware knowledge graph applications.

Major Research Projects

2025 – Present

Clinical and Translational Science Ontology Consortium (CTSOC)

University at Buffalo · CTSA Program Institutions

Role: Postdoctoral Research Associate / Ontologist. Developing formal ontologies to represent the translational research lifecycle and enable semantic interoperability and data integration across research phases and scientific, regulatory, and social contexts. (Project Wiki)

2021 – 2025

PeTWIN — Digital Twins for Petroleum Production Optimization and Management

UFRGS · University of Oslo · Petrobras (Libra Consortium) · Equinor

Role: Researcher / Lead Ontologist. Coordinated the ontology engineering team and led the modeling of offshore petroleum production assets, operational processes, and sensor information artifacts (resulting in the O3PO ontology) to support semantic data integration, data science pipelines, and automated reasoning. (petwin.org)

2018 – 2020

Digital Geosciences: Knowledge Management for the Energy Industry

UFRGS · SIRIUS Lab, University of Oslo

Role: Researcher. Modeled rock bodies, geological structures, and the processes governing their formation and evolution over geological time, combining terminology extraction from scientific literature with formal ontological analysis.
